verdict.rationale: The leave half of the story is reasonably supported. x402 is an open standard under vendor-neutral Linux Foundation governance described as 'free of lock-in to any one provider', with the SDK published on npm by the x402 Foundation. Sellers can receive at any address they control, including self-custody wallets, and buyers can pay from any signer. Settlement happens onchain, so payment records land on public chains, but no first-party export capability for account or facilitator data is documented. Missing for 10: a documented data-export feature for CDP/facilitator records, defined open export formats, an explicit procedure for migrating off the CDP facilitator, and independent or hands-on corroboration of exit.
